definition: To drink heartily. Not sip. Never sip.
Browned bread, or raising a glass to someone. Both go well with butter.
Hoofed mammal that stops a nation on the first Tuesday in November.
Neck warmer. Also a verb for inhaling your lunch.
Handheld light, and a must for any emergency kit. Americans call it a flashlight. We know better.
Grabbing the ball after a missed shot. Basketball was invented in 1891 by James Naismith, born on this day, and the first ‘hoops’ were peach baskets.
Small paddle boat. Reads the same backwards, gets you wet either way.
The darkest part of a shadow, where the light is completely blocked. Röntgen discovered X-rays on this day in 1895, and his first X-ray pictures were really shadows of bones.
Icy space rock that grows a glowing tail near the Sun. Carl Sagan, born today, co-wrote a whole book about them.
Living thing that makes its own food from sunlight. Water it, please.
Brass horn with no valves. It sounds the Last Post at dawn services.
Open paddle boat, pointed at both ends.
Feeling or showing gratitude. On World Kindness Day, being on the receiving end counts too.
Ten-armed sea creature. Calamari before it got crumbed.
A small, rounded hill. Usually grassy, occasionally grassy with conspiracy theories.
Green sauce of basil, pine nuts, garlic, hard cheese and olive oil, first made in Genoa.
What your face does when you get this in two guesses.
Sweet, sticky stuff bees make from nectar. It’s naturally antibacterial, so it turns up on some wound dressings.
Spherical map of the Earth. Spin it, point, book flights.
Spiny little insectivore that rolls into a ball when threatened. Not native to Australia; our spiky local is the echidna.
Very large. Named after a famous circus elephant.
Slow, marshy creek of the American South. Mind the alligators.
Baked dough. Also slang for money.
Small round fruit that grows in bunches. Wine in waiting.
Sweet tropical stone fruit. Summer's official mascot.
To ride a bike. Also anything that repeats in a loop. Today is Sustainable Transport Day.
Explosive patented by Alfred Nobel in 1867. He signed the will that created the Nobel Prizes on this day in 1895.
Small booth selling newspapers, snacks or tickets.
Flowering garden plant. Greek for 'flame'.
